item.title: HOOSER: The power of a council majority
item.description: While the voice of a single county councilmember can shine a light and nudge forward important changes in public policy, a majority of four can move mountains.

item.title: Zonta celebrates Women’s History Month, and International Women’s Day
item.description: LIHUE — The Zonta Club of Kauai will be partnering with the Habitat for Humanity on Saturday for a hands-on service project in observance of March being Women’s History Month, as well as the International Women’s Day on March 8.

item.title: Duo heading to Special Olympics Nationals
item.description: LIHUE — Special Olympics athlete Bradley Kaimana McDermott and Unified Partner Jonathan Anderson of the Kauai Police Department have been very consistent in showing up for bowling practice at the Kauai Bowl on Mondays.

item.title: Hawaii delegation continues to blast U.S. attack on Iran
item.description: Hawaii’s congressional delegation continued Monday to condemn the U.S.- Israel military strikes on Iran, calling them unauthorized and avoidable while the Hawaii Republican Party voiced full support for President Donald Trump’s actions.

item.title: Pearl Harbor survivor had returned for 60th anniversary
item.description: Clarence “Bud” R. Lane, 100, one of the last known service members who survived the Dec. 7, 1941, attack on Pearl Harbor died Feb. 21 at his home in Melbourne, Fla., surrounded by his family.

item.title: 32nd Annual Hoike Hula Concert Saturday
item.description: LIHUE — Na Hoku Hanohano Award winner and Grammy nominee Kumu Hula Leilani Rivera Low and her Halau Hula O Leilani will celebrate the 32nd annual Ho‘ike Hula Concert on Saturday at the Kauai War Memorial Convention Hall.

item.title: Hawaiian Home Lands rent-to-own prospect has few takers
item.description: The state Department of Hawaiian Home Lands hasn’t convinced many beneficiaries to take a new path to homeownership at a unique rent-to-own project despite more than $1 million in touted benefits.
